correctness.rationale: The first k=floor(n/2) factorial-code coordinates always lie <=k, so bulk surplus S_n is a sum of independent indicators from j>k; hence Var_Q(S_n)<=E_Q S_n. For mean <=n^(2/3), Chebyshev gives Q mass 1-o(1) in a window of width n^(5/12), while U mass there vanishes via the atomless weak limit S_n/sqrt(n)=>e(1/2). For mean >n^(2/3), Q mass concentrates above half its mean while U puts o(1) there by tightness. Both bounds uniform in all marginals. Mallows independently generated code is a special case. Small n=3..5 factorial-code surplus enumerations checked independently; finite tests not a substitute for the Brownian limit.
